ideas.idea: Sum over solutions, not one solution: privileged-proposal importance sampling (v22)
ideas.why: The cost to certify is -log2 alpha, alpha = the total probability of the student's successful trajectories; forcing a teacher trajectory certifies one of them, and every long program has many equivalent ones (names, formatting, order). Here the teacher never writes in the transcript: the student sees the teacher's trajectory as a private reference and writes 32 whole episodes of its own; each successful one is weighted P(actions)/q(actions) (scored with and without the reference) and the cost is -log2 of the mean weight, plus one forced-teacher particle as a floor. Certified by the auxiliary-variable bound (as answer_sir); tends to -log2 alpha itself as the proposal covers the student's successes. Running on the mid-size students.
ideas.result: Mid-size terminal-bench totals: Qwen3-4B 92 bits/task (v19g 98), Qwen3-1.7B 114 (118), Qwen3-8B 87 (89); Delphi never finishes a privileged episode and pays forcing + log2 33. tau: Qwen3-1.7B 112 on 5 tasks (v19g 121), Qwen3-4B worse than v19g. Wins exactly where the privileged student finishes episodes itself.

ideas.idea: Per-turn importance sampling (v23) and forcing the cheapest privileged variant (v24)
ideas.why: v23: v22 turn by turn (student, privileged student and the teacher's action as one mixture). v24: v19g, but the forced action is the cheapest accepted variant the privileged student writes.
ideas.result: Within +-5% of v19g for the mid-size students (v23 worse: its fixed teacher share costs ~1 bit a turn). The per-turn protocols have saturated: what remains is a few lines of knowledge (a regex, a binary record format), so the next gains have to come from what is injected.

ideas.idea: Single-program teacher trajectories for data-derived terminal outputs
ideas.why: Where answer-only loses (the output is computed from data the student must read), one command that computes and writes the output, instead of exploring step by step.
ideas.result: Never picked: costlier than the step-by-step teacher for every student (Qwen3-4B analyze-access-logs 91 vs 39 bits). Exploration puts the data in context for the next command to copy; the per-task pick keeps both answer-only and step-by-step where each is cheaper.

ideas.idea: The post-trained release as the proposal
ideas.why: Sample episodes and solutions from the release (Instruct / RL model), weight each success by P_base / P_release: an importance-sampling estimate of the base model's own -log2 alpha that needs no teacher text at all, efficient exactly where post-training made the task easy. The weights also say, task by task, how many bits post-training moved the base, which is Study B's question measured directly.
ideas.result: No gain: terminal-bench = forcing + log2 33 (the releases almost never solve a terminal task in the base's raw format); tau worse than v19g (Qwen3-4B 31 vs 19 bits/task) although the release solved 30-40% of its episodes, because the base finds whole release episodes 150-300 bits less likely (KL(release || base) per episode). For Study B: post-training moves the base 150-300 bits per episode, 3-10x what the base needs to succeed with the best injection (20-70 bits).

ideas.idea: Twisted SMC per turn with a learned success probe
ideas.why: v22 weights whole episodes, so weights collapse on long ones. Resampling particles after every turn (sequential Monte Carlo) keeps them alive; the twist is a value probe on the student's own hidden states, trained on its rollouts of other tasks, predicting success. Any twist keeps the estimate certified; a good one makes it approach -log2 alpha with few particles.

ideas.idea: Two-level self-search: the student writes its own plans
ideas.why: The student drafts K plans ('Plan:'), the oracle picks the plan under which it succeeds most (log2 K bits), then rejection sampling under that plan. Costs log2 K - log2 alpha_plan instead of -log2 alpha: knowledge the student can state but rarely acts on becomes cheap.

ideas.idea: Pointer injection into a public library
ideas.why: The teacher's message is an index into a fixed library of solved tasks (tau-bench's train split with gold actions, AoPS/MATH solutions, the other terminal-bench tasks): log2 |library| bits buy a complete worked example in context. Cheap whenever the student can transfer a pattern (tau exchange/return flows, file-recovery scripts). First on tau-bench (v26): 295 train-split sessions, a pointer costs 8.2 bits; the teacher points at the shortlisted example that makes its own trajectory cheapest for the student, then v19g.
ideas.result: tau (v26): Qwen3-0.6B 35.4 -> 27.7 bits/task, 1.7B 34.1 -> 28.8; 4B unchanged; 8B and 14B worse (14.9 -> 18.6): the pointer costs 8.2 bits and a worked session saves more only for students below ~4B. Sending it only where forcing says it pays (+1 bit) keeps most of the gain for weak students and narrows the loss for strong ones.

ideas.idea: Paid decoding reshaping
ideas.why: Sample from a tilted law (temperature below 1, min-p) and pay its exact log-ratio per token. Strong students solve far more often at low temperature, so the tilt's price plus rejection can undercut -log2 alpha at temperature 1, and the trade-off itself is a measurement of how peaked the student's competence is.

ideas.idea: A learned injector
ideas.why: Train a small policy, by RL across many tasks, that decides when to intervene and what to inject so as to minimize certified bits; the protocols so far are hand-designed rules.

ideas.idea: tau-bench on teacher trajectories for all 10 tasks, the cheapest per student
ideas.why: Opus trajectories cut tau costs about 1.7x on the 4 original tasks; the 6 added tasks still use tau-bench's gold actions; two verified variants per task (lean: Opus style; noted: a Thought before each write) plus the benchmark's; each student gets, per task, the one it is cheapest to be forced through (a deterministic choice: free, like the answer phrasings), then per turn (v19g)
ideas.result: Forcing: the lean teacher is 19-42% cheaper than tau-bench's actions for every model; the noted one (a Thought before each write) costs 2-3x more (picked 3 of 239 times). Per turn (v19g) on each student's cheapest: Qwen3-8B 29 -> 12 bits/task, Qwen3-0.6B 43 -> 32 (vs v19b on the benchmark actions); Spearman with release accuracy 0.97 (was 0.93), AUROC 0.69 (0.72), run-to-run 0.94. 4096-token models (Delphi, OLMo-2, Marin) fit only 2 of 10 tasks.

ideas.idea: Peer trajectories: other base models' own successful episodes as teacher variants
ideas.why: a trajectory written by a model is in a model's style, so it may be cheaper to force than Opus's or mine for similar students; 12 stronger base models x 32 unaided episodes on all 20 long-horizon tasks, recording every action (records so far kept only the last 3,000 characters); the verified successes join each student's per-task cheapest pick
ideas.result: 7,040 unaided episodes: 99 successes on 7 tau tasks, 6 on 2 terminal tasks; replay-verified peers are forced on every model, then each student's pick is redone and the per-turn protocol reruns where it changed

ideas.idea: Per-student teacher paraphrases
ideas.why: the teacher writes K verified-equivalent versions of each command and forces the one the student finds cheapest (a deterministic choice, certified like the answer phrasings); teacher text in the student's own style was the largest lever so far (3-5x)
ideas.status: partly done (tau: lean / noted / benchmark / peers)

ideas.idea: Answer-only teacher trajectories for terminal tasks
ideas.why: Most terminal bits go to exploration the teacher does not need: assign-seats spends ~90 bits reading clue files for a ~40-bit answer. A verified variant per task writes the output directly (a simpler regex for regex-log, the recovered values for sqlite), offered to each student's per-task pick next to the teacher, benchmark and peer trajectories; per turn (v19g) reruns where the pick changes.
ideas.result: Forced costs fall by a third over all 10 tasks and 30 bases (Qwen3-4B 96 -> 68 bits/task, Delphi-1e21 246 -> 163; assign-seats 134 -> 49, sqlite 205 -> 101 for Qwen3-4B); Delphi still monotone, Spearman with Qwen3 release accuracy 1.0, AUROC 0.873 -> 0.862. Per turn on top (v19g3) adds nothing (one command left).

ideas.idea: Teacher subgoal decompositions for all 10 terminal tasks (v20e/f/g)
ideas.why: subgoals beat the forced Opus trajectory on the original 3 tasks (Qwen3-8B 190 -> 112 with v20f); decompositions for the 7 added tasks split their teacher trajectories where the output shows a fact the rest needs (teachers/lh_subgoals_tb10.json); v20f and v20g on every base model, 2 runs

ideas.idea: A condensed tau-bench prompt for 4096-token models
ideas.why: the tau policy prompt alone takes ~2,650 of Delphi's 4096 tokens, so 8 of 10 tau tasks run out of context for Delphi, OLMo-2-7B and Marin-8B (an environment change: needs a decision)
ideas.result: Decided 2026-10-09 with the user: a 4,096-token context is too short for a standard tau-bench session, and a cut-down environment would not be standard. tau-bench is measured on long-context students (Qwen3 and the like); Delphi stays marked as out of context there.
